name: FENRIS INDUSTRIAL HullGrip Heavy Work Hand
product_name: FENRIS INDUSTRIAL HullGrip Heavy Work Hand
description:
The HullGrip is an oversized industrial prosthetic hand built from hardened tool-steel with a polyurethane outer shell rated for continuous heavy labor. Its hydraulic actuator system generates up to 180kg of grip force — sufficient to crush standard steel pipe — and the palm houses a switchable electromagnetic array capable of lifting up to 120kg of ferrous material. The hand is deliberately overbuilt: joints are rated for 2 million flex cycles, the shell is replaceable in the field, and internal components are modular enough for a mechanic with basic tools to service on a dock or construction site.

Fenris Industrial designed the HullGrip for their core customer base: Great Lakes dock workers, demolition crews, heavy machinery operators, and anyone whose job destroys conventional prosthetics within months. It is ugly, loud, and enormous — it extends the hand profile by roughly 30% compared to biological baseline — and Fenris makes no apology for any of that. Among Tier 1-2 labor communities it carries a specific prestige, and workers often customize the polyurethane shell with paint or engravings. Its magnetic palm makes it indispensable for working with ferrous components in low-visibility environments.
installation_requirements: Wrist or mid-forearm amputation; reinforced forearm skeletal anchoring recommended due to unit weight; 3-hour surgical fitting
rejection_risk: Low — mechanical socket interface; no bioelectric integration beyond basic EMG; socket liner requires regular replacement
maintenance: Hydraulic fluid check monthly; shell inspection and replacement as needed; magnetic coil servicing every 18 months

cultural_context: HullGrip hands are a common sight on Fenris work crews and Great Lakes cargo docks. Workers name their hands, paint them in crew colors, and engrave kill-counts of broken machinery onto the shells. The hand's crushing force has made it notorious in underground fighting circuits, where HullGrip users are often banned or placed in restricted brackets. Corporate security treats a visible HullGrip as an immediate threat assessment flag.
story_hooks: A series of industrial 'accidents' at a Fenris-contracted dock all involve workers whose HullGrip magnets activated without input, pulling them into machinery — someone has the override frequency
A HullGrip with a suspiciously high grip-force rating — far beyond spec — is circulating on the black market, and its origin traces back to a classified ARCTURUS field modification program
